problem: Find the angle between $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
Rearranging the dot product formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 4+4\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}}\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{16}{\sqrt{20}\cdot \sqrt{20}} \\  & =\frac{16}{20} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{4}{5})≈{36.87}^{∘}.
$$
